subject: Matemática
description_pt: Comparar e ordenar frações associadas às ideias de partes de inteiros, resultado da divisão, razão e operador.

components.description_pt: Interpretar fração em contextos de parte-do-todo, resultado de divisão, razão e operador
components.description_en: Interpret a fraction in the contexts of part-of-a-whole, division result, ratio, and operator
components.cc_component_description: Interpret a fraction as division of the numerator by the denominator (a/b = a ÷ b)

components.description_pt: Comparar duas frações interpretando-as dentro do mesmo contexto conceitual
components.description_en: Compare two fractions by interpreting them within the same conceptual context
components.cc_component_description: Compare two fractions with different numerators and different denominators

components.description_pt: Ordenar conjunto de frações associadas a significados de parte-do-todo, razão ou operador
components.description_en: Order a set of fractions associated with part-of-a-whole, ratio, or operator meanings
components.cc_component_description: Justify comparison of fractions with different numerators and different denominators

cc_matches.description: Compare two fractions with different numerators and different denominators, e.g., by creating common denominators or numerators, or by comparing to a benchmark fraction such as $\frac{1}{2}$. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two fractions refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with symbols >, =, or <, and justify the conclusions, e.g., by using a visual fraction model.

Interpret a fraction as division of the numerator by the denominator ($\frac{a}{b} = a \div b$). Solve word problems involving division of whole numbers leading to answers in the form of fractions or mixed numbers, e.g., by using visual fraction models or equations to represent the problem. *For example, interpret $\frac{3}{4}$ as the result of dividing 3 by 4, noting that $\frac{3}{4}$ multiplied by 4 equals 3, and that when 3 wholes are shared equally among 4 people each person has a share of size $\frac{3}{4}$. If 9 people want to share a 50-pound sack of rice equally by weight, how many pounds of rice should each person get? Between what two whole numbers does your answer lie?*
